items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: And I’m also pleased with what Mercer’s doing with Ellington’s band. And a lot of young players, we worked together at the Ohio State Fair.

ctx.x: And no one can quite put it into words, but there certainly is the feeling that you just expressed that that band just chugged along like no other.

It swings. Even today the orchestra is still — if I had my choice, if somebody was going to say to me, you have a choice of an 18-piece orchestra, I would today say the Basie band. So that’s great. And I’m also pleased with what Mercer’s doing with Ellington’s band. And a lot of young players, we worked together at the Ohio State Fair. The band was as crisp, if not more crisp, than I’ve ever heard that band. They really knocked me out. And we really have worked together more in the last five years I think than I…
I think they were scared to death not to, right?
